chunks: Corruption has spread over land and sea from what men have done themselves that they may taste a little of what they have done: They may haply come back (to the right path).
ai.seo_question: What is the cause of corruption spreading on land and sea according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a comprehensive diagnosis of both natural and social decay, linking environmental degradation directly to moral and spiritual negligence. The phrase 'taste some of what they have done' implies a tangible, experiential consequence rather than mere abstract punishment, serving as a catalyst for tawbah (repentance). This reflects the Shia understanding of the interconnectedness of human ethics and the physical world, where societal corruption manifests in ecological imbalance.
